tool_description: Control Unity VRM character with procedural gestures and emotions via WebSocket

available_gestures.name: wave
available_gestures.description: Wave at someone - raises right arm and waves hand

available_gestures.name: point
available_gestures.description: Point at a specific object or direction

available_gestures.name: reach
available_gestures.description: Reach toward an object to interact with it

available_gestures.name: nod
available_gestures.description: Nod head in agreement or acknowledgment

available_gestures.name: shake_head
available_gestures.description: Shake head to indicate no or disagreement

available_gestures.name: shrug
available_gestures.description: Shrug shoulders to indicate uncertainty or indifference

available_gestures.name: think
available_gestures.description: Thinking pose - hand near chin, head tilted

tool_usage_guidance: Use emotions to express feelings during conversation
Available emotions: happy, angry, sad, surprised, relaxed, neutral
Use gestures for physical actions and non-verbal communication
Gestures are procedural and goal-oriented - they adapt to the scene
Some gestures accept optional target parameters (object names in scene)
Examples: point at 'Cube', reach for 'Door', look at 'Camera'
Gestures execute with cooldown - wait for completion before next gesture
Combine gestures with emotions for richer expression
Use think gesture when contemplating or processing information
Use nod/shake_head for quick acknowledgment responses
Wave gesture is good for greetings and farewells
proactive_triggers: When user asks about physical objects in scene
When appropriate to gesture toward something specific
During explanations that benefit from physical demonstration

metadata.notes: Procedural gesture system with goal-oriented animations. Works with any humanoid VRM model. Gestures can target scene objects by name.
